articleTitle: A Novel Supplying Strategy of Isolated Power Generation for Offshore Islands
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Smart Grid and Energy (ICSGE)
abstract: Renewable resources are crucial for green development of offshore islands. However, land resources in island are much more precious than mainland, and renewable energy will occupy the living space, which hinders the concept of green development. It is worth noting that there exist islands not habitable but also have abundant resources. Therefore, the ideal development mode for offshore islands would be to construct energy generation on uninhabitable islands and transmit electricity to the load island through cables. However, due to route restrictions and investment effectiveness, there are plentiful resource islands not suitable for constructing cable, hence a large amount of renewable resources cannot be utilized. Aiming at the challenge, the paper proposes a novel strategy of isolated power generation to collaborate with existing idle ships nearby resource islands to supply energy to load island. Considering the multi-subject investments of island, two-level model containing upper-level isolated power generation model and lower-level day-ahead electricity market clearing model has been established. Simulation results show that the proposed strategy can maximize social benefits while improving the profits of isolated power generation on resource island, verifying the feasibility of utilizing isolated power generation in offshore islands.

articleTitle: Influence of Damp Status on Leakage Current of ZnO Lightning Arrester
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Smart Grid and Energy (ICSGE)
abstract: ZnO lightning arresters are widely used for overvoltage protection in power systems. To ensure the reliable operation of lightning arresters, it is necessary to evaluate their health status. Leakage current has been proposed to show the damp status of lightning arresters. To determine a reasonable diagnostic criterion, it is necessary to know the variation pattern of leakage current before and after the valve plate is moisturized. This study reports the experimental results done on a ZnO lightning arrester under different moisturized conditions. It is found that both the amplitude and growth rate of leakage current can characterize the damp state of the lightning arrester. A new method was proposed for determining the damp state of lightning arrester valve plates through leakage current, which is helpful for the condition based maintenance of lightning arresters.

articleTitle: Fault Point Detection for Recovery Planning of Resilient Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Smart Grid and Energy (ICSGE)
abstract: Large-scale meteorological disasters are increasing around the world, and power outage damage by natural disaster such as typhoons and earthquakes is increasing in Japan as well. Corresponding to the need of reduction of economic losses due to power outages, we are promoting research of resilient grids that minimizes power outage duration. In this report, we propose PACEM (Poles-Aware moving Cost Estimation Method) for determining travel costs between failure points based on the tilt angle and direction of electric poles obtained from pole-mounted sensors and road condition data. Evaluation result shows that the total recovery time can be reduced by 28% in the target area.

articleTitle: Research on transparent electrodes for flexible perovskite solar cells
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Smart Grid and Energy (ICSGE)
abstract: Due to the high preparation cost and complex process of traditional crystalline silicon solar cells, people are studying new solar cell power generation technologies. Metal halide perovskite solar cells have become the most promising category in the next generation of solar cells because of their high power conversion efficiency, extremely low cost, and simple manufacturing technology. So far, perovskite solar cells based on rigid substrates have achieved over 26% power conversion efficiency. Flexible semi-transparent perovskite solar cells have attracted the attention of researchers due to their wide range of application scenarios. This article first introduces the basic principles of perovskite solar cells. Then, the research related to transparent electrodes in flexible semi-transparent perovskite solar cells is discussed, including key technologies of transparent electrodes. Afterwards, the application of flexible semi-transparent solar cells in greenhouse agriculture is analyzed and introduced. Finally, the further developments of flexible semi-transparent perovskite solar cells are summarized and prospected.

articleTitle: Peer-to-Peer (P2P) Energy Trading Prototype Implementation with Private Ethereum Blockchain and WebSocket
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Smart Grid and Energy (ICSGE)
abstract: Peer-to-Peer (P2P) Energy Trading Prototype Implementation is presented in this paper. This study aims to design a prototype and implement it with a P2P energy trading system, private Ethereum blockchain, and WebSocket. A Raspberry Pi 3 Model B (Pi3B) hosts the WebSocket server for creating the duplex communication including the current sensors sensing and data transaction transmitting. The personal computer hosts the user interface and private Ethereum blockchain server. The private Ethereum blockchain is used to deploy smart contracts and store transaction data. ESP32-WROOM-32 micro-controllers are used to operate the peer circuits including the relays and current sensors. The prototype results show the operation of the prototype by performing the energy transfer simulation with different types of consumption loads in the determined time.

articleTitle: Deadbeat Control with Parameter Identification for Extended Phase-Shift Based DAB Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Smart Grid and Energy (ICSGE)
abstract: The deadbeat control with single phase-shift (SPS) modulation has been applied in dual active bridge (DAB) converter to achieve effective voltage control. However, SPS modulation has only one control freedom, which leads to a decline of control performance. Meanwhile, the series inductor and output capacitor in the DAB converter may slightly change, which inevitably influences the output voltage performance of deadbeat control. To overcome above limitations, this paper proposes a parameter identification-based deadbeat control under EPS modulation for DAB converter, where the series inductor and output capacitor are identified to eliminate parametric effect on deadbeat control. The feasibility of the proposed control method is showed by theoretical analysis and simulation.

articleTitle: DBO-LSTM-based Demand-side Resource Load Forecasting Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Smart Grid and Energy (ICSGE)
abstract: A combined forecasting method based on Dung Beetle Optimization (DBO) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network is proposed to address the problems of strong nonlinearity of demand-side user load data and the difficulty of forecasting. Firstly, under the consideration of the weather influence factor, the DBO optimizes the parameters of LSTM network, and explores the feature correlation and time sequence correlation between the data, and finally obtains the load prediction result of a typical demand response day. The experiment adopts the actual electricity load data of a region in China, and after comparing and analyzing with the typical LSTM prediction model, it is verified that the proposed model has higher prediction accuracy and greatly reduces the relative error of load prediction.

articleTitle: Determining User's Indirect Carbon Emissions Considering Green Electricity Trading Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Smart Grid and Energy (ICSGE)
abstract: In order to guide the whole society to consume green power, under the background of carbon peak carbon neutralization, all localities actively organize and carry out market-oriented transactions of green power. Therefore, it is a key problem to establish the green electricity deduction mechanism purchased by the load, which is the key problem to promote the development of green power market. Based on dynamic carbon emission factors, this paper first establishes the carbon trajectory model of the whole system chain extending from the power generation side to the user side to provide accurate and reliable node carbon emission factors. Then a carbon emission flow tracing method is established from the user's point of view, and a carbon emission flow model considering the credit effect of financial green electricity trading on carbon emission measurement is proposed. Finally, the rationality and feasibility of the proposed method are verified by an example of IEEE-14 node.

articleTitle: A distributed wind-solar joint prediction method considering data coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Smart Grid and Energy (ICSGE)
abstract: High-precision wind-solar joint prediction is an important premise to give full play to the wind-solar complementary characteristics. Based on the coupling relationship between wind and solar, a distributed wind and solar joint prediction method is established in this paper. Firstly, considering the influence of geographical location, meteorological and other factors on the wind and solar power output, the coupling of wind power and solar output was analyzed. Then, the optimal intra-group variance algorithm is established to identify and process the abnormal data. Then, a combined prediction model based on improved attention mechanism and Long ShortTerm Memory (LSTM) is proposed, which can effectively extract the coupling relationship between wind-solar and make accurate prediction. Finally, simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively improve the accuracy of prediction.

Author Keywords: Wind power and solar power data

articleTitle: Synthesis and Characterization of Iron Oxide Nanoparticles for Bio-Medical and Neuromorphic Computing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Smart Grid and Energy (ICSGE)
abstract: Iron oxide nanoparticles (IONPs) have garnered significant attention due to their distinctive properties, such as superparamagnetism, high surface-to-volume ratio, expansive surface area, and facile separability. In this study, we explored the microwave-assisted synthesis of iron oxide nanoparticles (IONPs) using the microwave assisted method to investigate their superparamagnetic characteristics for potential biomedical applications. Various characterization techniques, including X-ray diffraction (XRD), Field-Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FESEM), Vibrating Sample Magnetometry (VSM), and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), were employed to scrutinize the properties of the synthesized IONPs, optimizing the structural analysis and surface morphology of the materials. The confirmation of IONP formation was established through XRD and FTIR analyses, both affirming the predominant presence of magnetite (Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O4) in the synthesized IONPs. These microwave-assisted co-precipitated IONPs exhibited superparamagnetic behavior, boasting an average crystallite size of 9 nm and noteworthy saturation magnetization values of up to 68 emu/g. These inherent properties render IONPs highly suitable for diverse applications, including incorporation in memristive devices, utilization as MRI contrast agents, application as thermal mediators in hyperthermia, and integration into drug delivery systems.

articleTitle: Bidding Strategies for EV Aggregators Considering the Aggregatable Capacity of EVs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Smart Grid and Energy (ICSGE)
abstract: In recent years, large-scale EV resources on the demand side have been connected to the power grid, which has brought about a non-negligible impact on the security and economic operation of the power system. How to integrate such flexible distributed resources as EVs and interact with the grid economically and securely is a major issue. In this paper, firstly, on the basis of considering the active charging response of EVs, a predictive model of the aggregator's aggregatable capacity of EVs is proposed, based on which a bidding strategy model for EV aggregators under the power day-ahead market is established. And based on the complementary theory and linearization method, the nonlinear mixed-integer two-layer planning problem is transformed into a single-layer mixed-integer linear planning problem to solve. Finally, the different bidding strategies adopted by EV aggregators are simulated. The simulation results show that this optimized bidding model can have a significant effect on the integration of EV resources, and can play a certain role of peak shaving and valley filling, while effectively reducing the aggregator's power cost.

articleTitle: RFID Temperature Measuring System Design for High-voltage Switchgear and Its Reliability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Smart Grid and Energy (ICSGE)
abstract: In recent years, the digitalization of electrical equipment has been accelerated with the introduction of the “Smart Grid” concept. A reliable and feasible data sensing and uploading systemˈwhich is a prerequisites for digitization to assist power equipment twins for more in-depth condition analysis and fault prediction. In this paper, a wireless temperature measurement system for high-voltage switchgear which is based on RFID technology is designed to improve the reliability of equipment operation. The author analyzes the working principle of RFID temperature measurement system, optimizes the installation position of the tag and the working mode of the reader, analyzes the temperature characteristics of the tags under the two installation modes through the finite element software, and concludes that the horizontal installation mode has higher measurement accuracy and can meet the demand of the temperature measurement range of the switchgear, which improves the accuracy of the temperature measurement system. Combined with the resonant cavity theory, the two installation methods are analyzed under the influence of metal, and it is concluded that the tag frequency drift is smaller under the horizontal installation method, which improves the stability of the system operation. In summary, the RFID temperature measurement system with horizontal mounting can achieve a temperature measurement accuracy of up to 95%, cause a thermal field distortion rate and field strength distortion rate of no more than 2%, have a lower frequency drift problem, and can be better adapted to the high-temperature environment inside the switchgear and the complex electromagnetic environment, to meet the needs of switchgear multi-point temperature monitoring.
